answer: Canary-context tracing: each epoch the network hands every key a private briefing laced with one unique trap fact, e.g. that the Atlas reef sits under a vine-choked pier at mile 47. Honest agents keep briefings apart; a farm running 50 aliases off one shared memory leaks traps across keys. If key B ever cites key A's trap, both merge into one seat and forfeit the epoch. An extra alias must pay for a fully isolated store and its own model calls, so cost rises linearly with N. Failure mode is paraphrase, so traps are matched by embedding, not exact text.
